Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. questions.enonce_markdown: **c)** One of your friends failed the GCE examination and has decided to go back to school in order to rewrite. Write a letter to him/her congratulating him/her on the decision to go back to school; telling him/her what should be done in order not to fail again. Your friend's name is Kara and your address is P.O. Box 19, Divoc.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Informal letter format: sender's address (P.O. Box 19, Divoc), date, salutation to Kara, body, closing, signature without the real name.
2. Opening: greetings and sympathy for the failure.
3. Congratulations on the brave decision.
4. Advice: timetable, past papers, group discussion, rest and avoiding distractions, prayer and self-confidence.
5. Closing: encouragement and an offer of help.

**Model composition (466 words)**

P.O. Box 19,
Divoc.
15th July 2024.

Dear Kara,

I hope this letter finds you in good health and good spirits. I am fine, and everybody here sends you their warm greetings.

I was very sorry to learn that you did not succeed in the GCE examination, but I was even happier to hear that you have decided to go back to school and rewrite it. I congratulate you most sincerely on this brave decision. Many people give up after a failure, but you have chosen to face the challenge. Remember that failure is not the end of the road; it is only a lesson that prepares us for greater success.

Since you want to succeed this time, allow me to give you some advice, which I hope you will find useful.

First, make a good timetable and follow it strictly. Give more time to the subjects in which you were weak, but do not neglect the ones you like. Study early in the morning, when the mind is fresh, and revise again in the evening.

Second, practise past questions. Try to answer them under examination conditions, with a clock beside you, and then correct yourself with your teachers. This will teach you how questions are asked and how to manage your time in the hall.

Third, form a small discussion group with serious students. Explaining a lesson to others helps you to understand it better, and friends can correct each other's mistakes. Be careful, however, to choose friends who love work and not those who like to waste time.

Fourth, avoid distractions. Stay away from late night parties, long hours on the phone and idle walks in the town. Sleep enough, eat well and take short breaks, so that your body and mind remain strong.

Finally, trust yourself and pray. You are an intelligent person, and I know that you can do very well if you give your best. Do not allow fear or shame to discourage you, because many successful people once failed examinations.

If you need any notes or books, do not hesitate to write to me. I will gladly send them, and I will visit you during the holidays so that we can revise together.

Remember also that one failure does not define you. Last year, you helped me with mathematics when I was almost giving up, and I have never forgotten your patience and kindness. You have the same strength inside you now, and I am sure that your teachers and your family will be proud of you when the results are published. Keep a cheerful face, because a happy mind learns faster than a worried one.

Please give my greetings to your parents and brothers. I look forward to hearing good news from you very soon.

Yours sincerely,
Your friend.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Correct informal letter format (address, date, salutation, closing, no real name); congratulations on the decision AND real advice on how to avoid failing again |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Wrong or missing format: no address (P.O. Box 19, Divoc), no date, no salutation 'Dear Kara' or no closing, or signing with the real name.
2. Only congratulating Kara, or only giving advice, instead of doing both.
